description: A comprehensive overview of major international organizations, their headquarters, and primary functions. This topic is essential for understanding global governance, international diplomacy, and global economics.

sections.title: United Nations and its Principal Organs
sections.description: Introduction to the largest international organization dedicated to promoting global peace and cooperation.

key_concepts.explanation: An intergovernmental organization whose stated purposes are to maintain international peace and security, develop friendly relations among nations, and achieve international cooperation.
The main policy-making and deliberative organ of the UN, where all 193 member states have equal representation (one country, one vote).
Responsible for maintaining international peace. It has 15 members: 5 permanent (USA, UK, Russia, France, China) with veto power, and 10 non-permanent members elected for two-year terms.

historical_events.significance: Established after World War II to replace the ineffective League of Nations and prevent future global conflicts.

important_facts.fact: The headquarters of the United Nations (UN) is located in New York City, USA.

sections.title: Global Financial and Trade Institutions
sections.description: The primary organizations that govern the world economy, international trade, and monetary stability.

key_concepts.explanation: A historic gathering of 44 nations that led to the creation of the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund (IMF), jointly referred to as the 'Bretton Woods Twins'.

key_associations.extra_info: Provides long-term loans and grants to the governments of low- and middle-income countries for the purpose of pursuing capital and infrastructure projects.
Promotes global monetary cooperation, secures financial stability, and facilitates international trade by providing short-term balance of payments support.
Established in 1995 to regulate international rules of trade between nations. It officially replaced the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT).

sections.title: Major Geneva-based Organizations
sections.description: Crucial international bodies that are headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland.

key_associations.extra_info: A specialized agency of the UN responsible for international public health. It was established on April 7, 1948.
Focuses on advancing social and economic justice through setting international labour standards. It was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1969.
Facilitates international cooperation on the state and behavior of the Earth's atmosphere, climate, and water resources.
Promotes the protection of intellectual property (IP) rights worldwide, including patents, copyrights, and trademarks.

sections.title: Other Major Global Organizations
sections.description: Important global organizations headquartered in various other major cities across the world.

key_associations.item: UNESCO (UN Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization)
key_associations.extra_info: Promotes world peace and security through international cooperation in education, arts, sciences, and culture (e.g., declaring World Heritage Sites).
Provides humanitarian and developmental assistance to children and mothers in developing countries worldwide.
Leads international efforts to defeat hunger and improve nutrition and food security.
The principal judicial organ of the UN. It settles legal disputes submitted by member states in accordance with international law.
Coordinates the UN's environmental activities and assists developing countries in implementing environmentally sound policies.

sections.title: Exam-Oriented Important Facts
sections.description: High-yield, direct facts frequently asked in competitive exams regarding international organizations.

important_facts.fact: World Health Day is celebrated globally on April 7 every year to commemorate the establishment of the World Health Organization (WHO) in 1948.
The International Court of Justice (ICJ) consists of 15 judges who are elected to 9-year terms by the UN General Assembly and the Security Council.
The Asian Development Bank (ADB), established in 1966 to foster economic growth and cooperation in the Asia-Pacific region, is headquartered in Manila, Philippines.
The South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) was established in 1985 and its secretariat is based in Kathmandu, Nepal.
INTERPOL (The International Criminal Police Organization), which facilitates worldwide police cooperation and crime control, is headquartered in Lyon, France.
